title: Very tame action on an fs log scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme with log morphisms, geometric stalks and nonunit ideals as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$ as in [def-per-fs-log-group-action]. The action is very tame if it is tame and, for every geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, its inertia group acts trivially on $\overline M_t=M_t/\mathcal O_{X,t}^{\times}$ and on $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{X,t}/I_t)$, where $I_t$ is the nonunit log ideal. Explicitly, for every inertia element and every pointed relative etale diagram representing its pullback, each log section and its pullback have associated germs (differ by a unit), and every regular function and its pullback have germs differing by an element of $I_t$. These tests on all germs specify the actual action on the characteristic monoid and strict local stratum.

Blueprint search: no very-tame match; Kummer hits concern coefficient sheaves and do not define these geometric notions.
mathlib_searches.verdict: new general notions needed; reuse FSLogGroupAction and FSLogSmoothEtale

Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: equivariant modification X double-prime and log-smooth quotient X double-prime/H. Supporting construction and local calculations in ILO VIII 4--5 and X 1.2--1.8. In this quotient lemma: the very-tame hypothesis and Kummer characteristic and standard-chart conclusions.

reviewed_lean.note: Checked ILO VI 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.5 and proof 3.7 clause by clause. Conclusions: exists Y and q; Noetherian, finite, surjective; IsQuotient (invariant rings, M_Y=(q_*M)^G on etale tests, injective log pullback); geometric orbit fibres on Spec Omega points; Y log regular; IsLogEtale; IsKummer (ILO 2.1); HasStrictLocalKummerChart at every geometric point (fs stalk charts, ring map pinned on germs, injective Kummer h, finite cokernel killed by a d invertible on O^sh_Y, IsPullback correctly oriented, as in ILO 2.2/3.5(c)); unique EtaleLogHom factorization of invariant maps (uniqueness follows from log_injective).
